newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST-Next Swedish repo rate cut seen Dec 17.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Next Swedish repo rate cut seen Dec 17.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, was expected to leave its repurchase rate unchanged at its regular tender on Tuesday, but to cut the rate on December 17, a poll of 10 analysts showed.
"There is room for a cut but the Riksbank will probably wait until the inflation report is released on December 17," one economist told Reuters.
Forecasts for the December 17 cut varied from five basis points to 25, but most forecasts ranged between 10 to 20 points.
Two of the 10 analysts said the Riksbank would cut the rate tomorrow at its regular repo tender at 0830 GMT.
"The Riksbank has surprised the market lately. It's beginning to take after the German central bank," one economist said.

The economists surveyed said the repo rate was close to bottoming out. Several said it would hit bottom in January, while others said it would happen sometime in the first quarter when the rate hit between 3.75 and four percent.
The average for the bottom repo rate was 3.90 percent.
The repo rate, the key rate which moves within the central bank's interest rate corridor, currently stands at 4.35 percent.
The corridor's floor, or deposit rate, is 3.75 percent and its ceiling, or lending rate is 5.25 percent since a widely-expected 50 basis point cut last Thursday.

Sources who participated in this survey were from Carnegie, Consensus, Hagstromer & Qviberg, PaineWebber, Paribas Capital Markets, S-E-Banken, Sparbanken, Union Bank of Switzerland, Unibank Markets, and Ohman Fondkommission.
